learning: Iteration 3 (80 mm row, 0.12 m track) gave the best score so far with max_error near 0.062 m. If the narrower track raises effective steering gain, kp should fall; if steering_oscillation rises, kd is the next lever. Iteration 1 (narrow track with lighter robot and changed sensors) is confounded and gives no clean track evidence.
notes: Adopts the Builder's 0.10 m track and 80 mm row unchanged and lowers kp from 0.8 to 0.7 to offset the roughly 20 percent higher turn gain from the narrower track. kd, ki, base_speed and line-loss handling match the best run (iteration 3, score 69.18).
rationale: Iteration 3 (80 mm row, 0.12 m track, kp 0.8, kd 0.15) scored 69.18, the best so far. Max error sat at 0.062 to 0.067 m on all tracks while RMS stayed at 0.019 to 0.033 m, so the failure is a transient peak at bends. The Builder's proposal narrows wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m, which by the contract's turn-rate formula (vR - vL)/track raises the turn rate per unit PWM difference by about 20 percent. The effective steering gain therefore rises by about the same amount. Iteration 1 showed that a narrower track with a lighter robot did not improve the score, but it changed mass, sensor size and pitch too, so it does not isolate the track effect. I keep the geometry exactly as proposed and scale the controller to the higher gain: kp falls from 0.8 to 0.7 (about 12 percent, a little less than the 20 percent gain rise, to avoid overcorrecting into oscillation). kd stays at 0.15 because iteration 3 showed no sign of excess jitter (steering_oscillation 0.12 to 0.17), and it is the damping term that the Builder's integrator question asks about. ki stays at 0 because no steady offset has been observed. base_speed stays at 1.5 and line_loss stays last_direction, both unchanged from the best run. Expected result, not yet measured: max_error near 0.06 m and a score above 69. The main risk is extra oscillation on the s-bend and slalom if the effective gain still rises more than kp falls.
